triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '4. cute.compile warm call drops Constexpr args — pass only tensors + Int32' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 4. cute.compile warm call drops Constexpr args — pass only tensors + Int32

problem.statement: GDN Chunk Forward Pitfalls (CuTeDSL, SM120) -- 4. cute.compile warm call drops Constexpr args — pass only tensors + Int32

payload.attempted: You pass `cutlass.Constexpr[int]` values (T, H, HV, etc.) to the compiled kernel's warm call, matching the cold compile signature.
payload.lesson: Cold compile: pass everything (tensors + Int32 + Constexpr). Warm call: pass ONLY tensors + Int32, in the same order, omitting all Constexpr args.

established_fact.mechanism: `cute.compile` captures all `Constexpr[...]` values at compile time and eliminates them from the runtime signature. The warm call only accepts runtime arguments: `cute.Tensor` (via `from_dlpack`) and `cutlass.Int32`.

payload.observed: Silent garbage output or crash. The warm call ignores Constexpr args entirely — they were baked into the compiled kernel during `cute.compile`. Extra positional args shift tensor bindings.
payload.root_cause: `cute.compile` captures all `Constexpr[...]` values at compile time and eliminates them from the runtime signature. The warm call only accepts runtime arguments: `cute.Tensor` (via `from_dlpack`) and `cutlass.Int32`.

implementation.snippet:
```python
# Cold compile
compiled = cute.compile(launch_fn, mK, mQ, mO, cutlass.Int32(B), T, H, NT)
# Warm call — no T, H, NT
compiled(mK, mQ, mO, cutlass.Int32(B))
```
